title: Separation of Small and Large Extracellular Vesicles from Cardiac Tissues
author: Liang, Najor, et al.
materials: Pierce Bradford Plus Protein Assay Kit

This section describes the separation of EVs from each fraction using antibodies against specific proteins that are present on the surface of the vesicles (Figure 3). We use the EV Isolation Kit Pan (human or mouse, Miltenyi Biotec) containing magnetic MicroBeads cross linked to antibodies recognizing tetraspanin proteins CD9, CD63, and CD81 for this step. However, there are alternative antibody-conjugated beads from other companies (e.g., Thermo Fischer Scientific, Abcam, System Biosciences) that are using the same principle and can be used for the immunoaffinity purification of EVs.32.Add 50 μL of EV Isolation MicroBeads Pan (EV Isolation Kit Pan mouse or human, Miltenyi Biotec) recognizing the specific tetraspanin proteins, CD9, CD63 or CD81, to each tube containing 500 μL of EVs from steps #27 and #31.33.Transfer tubes to a benchtop tube rotator (Barnstead Rotator Model 415110) at 4°C and incubate 12–16 h (Figure 3A).34.The next morning, prewarm the Equilibration Buffer and Isolation Buffer to 18°C–20°C for 30 min.Note: These buffers are components of the EV Isolation Kit Pan from Miltenyi Biotec and should be stored at 4°C.35.Prepare the columns. Place the MACS columns in the magnetic field of the MACS Separator attached to a MACS MultiStand (Figures 3B and 3D).36.Add 100 μL Equilibration Buffer to the columns.37.Rinse the columns with 3 × 100 μL Isolation Buffer.Note: Make sure no buffer is remaining in the column reservoir before adding more buffer for the next rinse. However, it is important to never let the column run dry.38.Retrieve the samples from the tube rotator at 4°C that have been incubated 12–18 h and add the solution to the columns.Note: Magnetically labeled EVs will be retained on the columns while material not bound to magnetic beads will flow through.39.Wash the columns with 4 × 200 μL of Isolation Buffer.Note: For each wash - make sure no buffer is remaining in the column reservoir before adding more Isolation Buffer.40.Remove the columns from the magnetic separator and place each column onto a 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube.41.Add 65–100 μL of Elution Buffer (can be PBS or Western Blot Lysis Buffer, depending on the experimental plan for the EVs) and immediately elute the EVs by firmly pushing down the plunger (Figures 3C and 3E).Note: The eluate contains the EVs and is used for further analysis.Pause point: EVs eluted in Western Blot Lysis Buffer can be stored at −80°C for up to 1 year.CRITICAL: The isolated EVs eluted in PBS should not be subjected to freeze and thaw cycles. It is advisable to use them immediately or store at 4°C for no more than 24 h. Additionally, small EVs generally exhibit greater stability than large EVs, allowing them to be more durable at 4°C.Note: We have also used differential centrifugation combined with affinity purification to separate large and small EVs from plasma and from conditioned media collected from cultured cells. However, keep in mind that the amount of EVs secreted varies between cell lines and tissues. For example, EV secretion is increased in various cancer cell lines6 and in cells with compromised lysosomal function.1 The digestion time for other tissues also needs to be optimized. We find that 45 min is sufficient to digest heart tissue, while brain tissue from mice only requires 20 min of digestion.7Figure 3Overview of immunoaffinity purification of EVs(A) MicroBeads are added to large and small EV fractions and incubated for 12–16 h at 4°C.(B) Magnetically labeled EVs are retained within the column in the magnetic field.(C) EVs are eluted by removing columns from the magnetic field and adding PBS or Western Blot lysis buffer. A plunger is used to push through liquid and elution of EVs into an Eppendorf tube.(D) MACS columns attached to a MACS MultiStand.(E) A plunger attached to a column for elution of EVs.(F) EVs eluted in Western Blot lysis buffer.

It is highly recommended that the isolated EVs are evaluated by Westen Blot analysis to confirm the presence of standard EV markers, such as tetraspanins (CD9, CD63, CD81), Alix, and/or Tsg101 (Figure 4C).72.Elute large and small EVs from the columns (see step #41) in 65 μL Western Blot Lysis Buffer.73.Place on ice for 45 min to allow complete solubilization of vesicles.74.Save 5 μL from each sample to assess protein concentration using a Bradford Assay.75.Dilute samples in 4× LDS sample buffer (Novex by Life Technologies) and DTT (50 mM final concentration) to the sample, ensuring thorough mixing by vortexing.76.Heat at 95°C for 5 min in a heat block to denature proteins.77.After heating, briefly spin tubes in a microcentrifuge.78.Assemble polyacrylamide gel(s) in the electrophoresis apparatus and fill with NuPAGE MOPS SDS Running Buffer.79.Load molecular weight marker and samples onto the gel with appropriate percentage for the molecular weights of the proteins of interest.Note: We use the Invitrogen NuPAGE Novex gel system and we find that pre-made 12% gels allows for separation of the standard EV proteins. We also usually load 20–30 μg/well of heart lysates and EVs.80.Run gel at 180 V for about 60 min or until the dye reaches the bottom of the gel.81.Transfer proteins onto a nitrocellulose membrane.a.Soak sponges, Whatman filter paper and the nitrocellulose membrane in transfer buffer.b.Prepare the transfer sandwich by layering the components. From bottom to top: 3 sponges → 2 filter papers → membrane → gel → 2 filter papers → 3 sponges.c.Place the sandwich into the transfer cassette.d.Fill the cassette with cold transfer buffer and partially fill the transfer box with additional transfer buffer.82.Transfer for 150 min at 30 V at 4°C (in a cold room or refrigerator).83.When the transfer is complete, stain the membrane with Ponceau S for 5 min, then rinse in ddH2O.84.Capture a picture of the total proteins before completely rinsing off the stain with Tris-buffered saline+0.05% Tween 20 (TBST).Note: The Ponceau S stain allows for staining of total protein levels and can be used to compare the level of EV secretion between samples. This can be useful if comparing two conditions such as young vs aged tissues.85.Block membrane with TBST+5% non-fat milk for 1 h at 18°C–20°C.86.Incubate the membrane with the primary antibody against EV markers of choice for 12–18 h at 4°C on a rocker.Note: Primary antibodies are usually prepared at 1:1000 in TBST+5% non-fat milk. The optimal incubation time will depend on the antibody and should be determined empirically.87.The next morning, wash the membrane 3 × 10 min with TBST on a rocker at 18°C–20°C.Note: The washing steps are important to reduce non-specific background. Also, it is important to make sure that the membrane remains moist at all steps.88.Incubate membrane with the appropriate secondary antibody for 1 h at 18°C–20°C.Note: Secondary antibodies are usually prepared at 1:5000 in TBST+5% non-fat milk.89.Wash the membrane 3 × 10 min with TBST on a rocker at 18°C–20°C.90.Add a substrate for detecting the antibody bound to the protein.Note: We use Enhanced chemiluminescence (ECL) (Thermo Fisher Scientific) for detection of proteins.91.Visualize and capture proteins on the membrane in a ChemiDoc Imaging System or equivalent.

steps.title: Prepare buffers, tools and pre‑chill equipment
steps.instruction: Make all required buffers (including Digestion Buffer: HBSS + Liberase DH 200 µg/mL + DNase I 20 U/mL) and keep them on ice at 4 °C; sterilize tools, tissue‑culture plates and tubes, keep everything on ice; pre‑chill centrifuges and rotors at 4 °C for 12–18 h.

steps.title: Prepare frozen cardiac tissue
steps.instruction: Handle frozen human heart tissue on dry ice, trim if needed, and use at least 100–120 mg per sample; place tissue in a 100 mm dish on ice with ice‑cold HBSS, keep on ice for dissection, and optionally set aside 50–100 µg for Western blot (load 20–30 µg per lane).

steps.title: Filter digested tissue and perform differential centrifugation
steps.instruction: Separate large and small EV fractions by sequential filtration and centrifugation steps.

substeps.instruction: Place a 70 µm cell strainer over a 50 mL centrifuge tube and filter the digested tissue; rinse the dish with 5 mL HBSS and add the rinse to the strainer.
Centrifuge the filtrate at 300 × g, 4 °C for 10 min (Eppendorf 5810R) to pellet cells/debris; carefully pour supernatant into a clean 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge supernatant at 2,000 × g, 4 °C for 20 min to remove smaller cells/apoptotic bodies.
Set up a 10 mL syringe with a 0.8 µm cellulose‑acetate filter on top of an ultra‑clear tube; filter the supernatant and add 3 mL cold HBSS to avoid clogging.
Balance the tubes (weigh each, add cold HBSS to the lighter tube).
Pre‑chill the ultracentrifuge rotor and adaptors for 12–18 h at 4 °C.

Centrifuge at 16,500 × g, 4 °C for 25 min to pellet the large EV fraction (≈200–800 nm). Note: any centrifuge that can hold ≥8 mL tubes and reach 16,500 × g is acceptable; k‑factor of 32 Ti rotor = 204.
Decant supernatant without disturbing the large‑EV pellet; resuspend the pellet in 500 µL ice‑cold PBS, transfer to a 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube and keep on ice.
Weigh the tubes containing the remaining supernatant (small‑EV fraction) and add HBSS to balance.
Centrifuge at 118,000 × g, 4 °C for 150 min to pellet small EVs (≈50–200 nm).

Discard supernatant, place tubes upside‑down on a paper towel for 1–2 min, use a Kim‑Wipe to soak residual liquid, then resuspend each small‑EV pellet in 500 µL ice‑cold PBS and transfer to 1.7 mL tubes on ice.

steps.title: Immunoaffinity purification of EVs
steps.instruction: Capture CD9/CD63/CD81‑positive EVs from the large‑ and small‑EV suspensions using Miltenyi magnetic MicroBeads.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL EV Isolation MicroBeads Pan (Miltenyi) to each tube containing 500 µL of EV suspension (large‑EV and small‑EV fractions).
Place tubes on a benchtop rotator (Barnstead Rotator Model 415110) at 4 °C and incubate 12–16 h.
The next morning, pre‑warm Equilibration Buffer and Isolation Buffer to 18–20 °C for 30 min (store buffers at 4 °C until use).
Insert MACS columns into the magnetic field of a MACS Separator on a MultiStand.
Add 100 µL Equilibration Buffer to each column.
Rinse each column 3 × 100 µL Isolation Buffer, ensuring no buffer remains in the reservoir and the column never runs dry.
Retrieve the bead‑bound EV samples from the rotator (still at 4 °C) and apply each to a prepared column; magnetically labeled EVs will be retained.
Wash each column 4 × 200 µL Isolation Buffer, again avoiding dry columns and ensuring the reservoir is empty before the next wash.
Remove columns from the magnet and place each onto a fresh 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube.
Add 65–100 µL Elution Buffer (PBS or Western‑Blot Lysis Buffer) and firmly push the plunger to elute the EVs.
Store eluates in PBS on ice (use immediately or keep ≤24 h at 4 °C; avoid freeze‑thaw) or, if eluted in Lysis Buffer, store at –80 °C for up to 1 year.

steps.title: Nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA)
steps.instruction: Measure concentration and size distribution of the purified EVs using a NanoSight NS300.

substeps.instruction: Elute large and small EVs from the MACS columns in 100 µL cold PBS (see step 41).
Dilute 20 µL of each eluate in 1 mL PBS (keep on ice). For heart samples >100 mg, use a 1:50 dilution; for larger samples, start with 1:100.
Turn on the NanoSight NS300, allow it to warm up, and launch the NTA software.
Rinse the sample chamber and tubing sequentially with 70 % ethanol then PBS.
Load the diluted sample into a 1 mL syringe and insert it into the instrument inlet, avoiding bubbles.
Set camera level to 13 and detection threshold to 5.
Acquire three 60‑second videos per sample.
Analyze the videos, generate histograms, and export raw data (Excel) and a PDF report.
After each sample, flush the chamber with PBS; when finished, clean the chamber and tubing with 70 % ethanol followed by ddH₂O, close the software and switch off the instrument.

steps.title: Negative‑stain electron microscopy
steps.instruction: Prepare EVs for transmission EM by negative staining with uranyl acetate.

substeps.instruction: Elute large and small EVs from the columns in 100 µL cold PBS.
Glow‑discharge carbon‑coated EM grids to reduce hydrophobicity.
Place a piece of Parafilm (paper side up) on the bench.
Pipet 5–20 µL of the EV sample onto the Parafilm.
Using a microsurgery tweezer, place the grid carbon‑side down onto the drop and incubate ≥5 min.
Add three drops of ddH₂O (filtered through a 0.22 µm syringe filter) onto the Parafilm.
Transfer the grid (carbon side down) to the first water drop for 30 s, then to the second and third drops for 30 s each.
Dispense two drops of 2 % uranyl acetate (UA) in water onto the Parafilm; the first drop should be smaller than the second.
Place the grid carbon‑side down onto the first UA drop for 3 s, then onto the second larger UA drop for 1 min.
Fold a piece of filter paper in half; lift the grid vertically from the second UA drop to retain a large UA droplet on the grid.
Blot the grid edge onto the filter paper for 5 s.
Air‑dry the grid by holding it with tweezers for ~20 min (or until no liquid is visible).
Remove residual UA with a small piece of filter paper, place the grid in a grid‑box, and image on a JEOL JEM‑1400Plus (or equivalent) TEM.
Analyze particle size using ImageJ.

steps.title: Western blot analysis of EV proteins
steps.instruction: Detect EV markers by SDS‑PAGE and immunoblotting.

substeps.instruction: Elute large and small EVs from the columns in 65 µL Western‑Blot Lysis Buffer.
Incubate on ice for 45 min to solubilize vesicles.
Save 5 µL of each eluate for a Bradford protein assay.
Add 4× LDS sample buffer and DTT to a final concentration of 50 mM; vortex to mix.
Heat samples at 95 °C for 5 min, then briefly spin in a microcentrifuge.
Assemble a 12 % pre‑cast polyacrylamide gel (Invitrogen NuPAGE) in the electrophoresis chamber and fill with NuPAGE MOPS SDS Running Buffer.
Load a molecular‑weight marker and 20–30 µg of each sample per well; run at 180 V for ~60 min until the dye front reaches the bottom.
Prepare the transfer sandwich (3 sponges → 2 filter papers → nitrocellulose membrane → gel → 2 filter papers → 3 sponges) and place in a transfer cassette.
Fill the cassette and the surrounding transfer box with cold transfer buffer; perform wet transfer for 150 min at 30 V, 4 °C.
Stain the membrane with Ponceau S for 5 min, rinse with ddH₂O, and capture a total‑protein image.
Block the membrane in TBST + 5 % non‑fat milk for 1 h at 18–20 °C.
Incubate with primary antibody (typically 1:1000 in TBST + 5 % milk) against EV markers (e.g., CD9, CD63, CD81, Alix, Tsg101) for 12–18 h at 4 °C on a rocker.
Wash membrane 3 × 10 min with TBST at 18–20 °C.
Incubate with secondary antibody (typically 1:5000 in TBST + 5 % milk) for 1 h at 18–20 °C.
Wash 3 × 10 min with TBST.
Add enhanced chemiluminescence (ECL) substrate and detect signal using a ChemiDoc imaging system (or equivalent).

description: To isolate EVs from mouse hearts and human cardiac tissue, we applied two sequential methods: differential centrifugation to separate the large (∼200–800 nm) and small (∼50–200 nm) EV fractions followed by immunoaffinity purification using antibodies conjugated to magnetic beads for further separation of the vesicles.1.Before you begin the isolation procedure, it is important that all the essential buffers have been prepared and chilled to 4°C.2.You also need to have sterilized tools, tissue culture plates, and various tubes set up at the appropriate workstations. Keep everything on ice or at 4°C, unless stated otherwise.3.Centrifuges and rotors should be prechilled to 4°C for 12–18 h before they are used.4.Prepare Digestion Buffer (Hanks Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS) plus Liberase DH (200 μg/mL) and DNase I (20 U/mL)) on the day of the procedure and maintain on ice until use.Note: All incubations are performed at 4°C unless otherwise noted.
